what: Same-host cost of the engine checker's decoding (matters_core::crdt::isolation::decode, which is the receiver's own decoding of a member's engine bytes and more) for the largest honest updates and for honest snapshots of growing collections, from which the checker's budgets are chosen
source_commit: branch core/engine-isolation, built on cc4f89c; the commits it was then rebased onto (#265, #266, #268) do not change the decoding measured
method: Each blob is written to a file and decoded in a fresh process, which reads it first, as the checker's child does. address_space_growth is VmPeak after decoding less VmSize before it: what RLIMIT_AS must allow on top of the child's own address space. resident_peak is VmHWM, the whole process included. cpu_seconds is user and system time from /proc/self/stat, in 10 ms ticks.

host.name: betelgeuse
host.conditions: shared development host with other sessions building; no CPU pinning; one run per workload, so wall time is not a measure of the decoding alone

workloads.update-creates: one commit creating tasks with titles only, as large as fits in 1 MiB (MAX_PLAINTEXT_BYTES)
workloads.update-notes: one commit creating a task with notes of about 1 MiB
workloads.update-renames: one commit creating a task and renaming it again and again, as many times as fit in 1 MiB
workloads.update-moves: one commit creating tasks and moving each to the top, as many as fit in 1 MiB
workloads.snapshot-words-N: N tasks, each created in its own commit with 1 KiB notes of varied words; every second renamed and every tenth completed, each its own commit
workloads.snapshot-repeated-N: as snapshot-words-N, with notes of 1 KiB of one repeated letter, which LZ4 compresses furthest

budgets.update: 256 MiB of address space and 10 s of processor time per update; the most an honest update took is 48.5 MiB and 0.42 s (update-renames): 5.3 and 24 times that
budgets.snapshot: 512 MiB plus 96 MiB per MiB of snapshot, and 10 s plus 2 s per MiB; the most memory for its size was snapshot-titles-100000 (16.4 MiB, 793 MiB, 12.3 s), allowed 2,144 MiB and 44 s: 2.7 and 3.6 times that
budgets.both: the wall clock allows the start, and each blob 20 s beyond twice its processor budget; no budget is more than half the machine's memory

findings: Memory grows with the collection, not the snapshot's bytes: about 8 KiB per task without notes and 11 to 12 KiB with 1 KiB notes, so the ratio of memory to snapshot size depends on how far the content compresses (10 times for varied words, 33 for repeated letters, 48 for titles only).
An honest 1 MiB update took at most 48.5 MiB; one holding a single large text took 2 MiB.
Processor time is about 0.12 to 0.15 s per 1,000 tasks of a snapshot on this host.
